title: Thin adaptor typed snippets & optimistic tool handshake — PRD (draft)
content:
Purpose

This doc captures a compact product proposal and engineer-facing runbook for a lightweight client adaptor that:
- serves as the default low-footprint SDK surface for progressive/streamed structured output;
- provides a typed-snippet framing to let clients receive interoperable fragments (JSON snippets, typed blocks) while streaming;
- introduces an optimistic tool-handshake where the server signals likely tool intent early in the stream so clients can prepare resources or fallbacks without blocking the main token path.

Why this?
- Many customers want streaming partial structured outputs (e.g., cards, proto snippets, mini-JSON) that can be consumed by UI renderers or tool runners incrementally.
- Full tool-call contracts and heavy serialization are heavyweight for mobile/edge clients.
- A thin adaptor enables fast onboarding: small surface area, predictable behavior, clear failure modes, and low bandwidth.

Goals (success criteria)
- Developer onboarding: end-to-end sample app that integrates typed snippets + optimistic tool handshake in <30 mins.
- Runtime: 95th percentile added latency <= 10ms overhead vs current streaming baseline for small responses.
- Safety & consistency: structured snippet schema mismatch rate < 0.5% for curated prompts in internal eval set.
- Rollout: progressive opt-in (feature flag) with telemetry to evaluate usage and error rates.

Non-goals
- This is not a full transactional tool protocol (no guaranteed exactly-once semantics).
- Not intended to replace full typed-tool-call PRDs that require durable commit/rollbacks.

User stories
- Mobile product engineer: receives incremental UI-ready card fragments so the app can render partial results while the model continues.
- Platform integrator: wants to pre-warm and sandbox a local tool runner when the model indicates high confidence an external API will be required.
- Server-side connector: can batch optimistic tool signals across sessions to prefetch auth tokens and avoid cold starts.

Design overview
1) Stream framing
- Each stream message (chunk) is one of: free-text, typed-snippet, optimistic-tool-signal, heartbeat.
- typed-snippet is a compact JSON-LD-like fragment with: id, schema, confidence_hint, payload (minified).
- optimistic-tool-signal is a small structured hint: {tool_id, intent_label, confidence, optional_metadata_url}.
- Server may emit optimistic-tool-signal early (pre-toolcall) and later emit a canonical typed-snippet with final tool-call or result.

2) Typed-snippet semantics
- Schema discovery: client may pass a small schema whitelist in the request (schema ids). Server prefers those schemas and will tag typed-snippet.schema accordingly.
- Idempotency: typed-snippet.id can be used by clients to dedupe repeated fragments.
- Partialness: a typed-snippet may be marked partial=true and include a continuation pointer. Clients should render partial fragments gracefully.

3) Optimistic tool handshake
- When the model execution path indicates an external tool is likely, runtime emits optimistic-tool-signal with a confidence float (0.0-1.0).
- The SDK layer exposes a callback: onOptimisticToolSignal(signal) that returns one of {prepare, ignore, throttle}.
- prepare: client can pre-warm credentials, open sockets, allocate ephemeral containers. This must be best-effort and cancelable.
- If the later stream never emits a canonical tool-call, pre-warm should be torn down after a short TTL.

API sketches (request-level)
- request body fields (new):
  - typed_snippet_whitelist: ["schema.cards.v1","schema.persona.v2"]  // optional
  - optimistic_tool_mode: "enabled|disabled|onDemand"
  - snippet_mode: "minified|expanded"

- response (stream) chunk envelope (text-first payload preserved):
  - {type: "typed-snippet", id: "s-124", schema: "schema.cards.v1", confidence_hint: "0.84", payload: "{\"title\":\"...\"}"}
  - {type: "optimistic-tool-signal", tool_id: "search-v2", intent_label: "lookup_firmographics", confidence: "0.72", metadata_url: "https://.."}

SDK ergonomics (principles)
- Minimal surface: two high-level callbacks in the streaming client: onSnippet(chunk) and onOptimisticTool(signal).
- Non-blocking defaults: callbacks must be async and not stall token emission. Default implementations are no-ops.
- Controlled pre-warm: provide a lightweight PrewarmController that exposes cancel(), ttl, and cost_estimate to avoid unexpected charges.
- Fallbacks: client helper to map optimistic-tool-signal -> local stub that can be used if final tool-call fails.

Developer flows and examples
- Mobile quick-start: 12-line snippet showing request with typed_snippet_whitelist and optimistic_tool_mode=enabled, then an onSnippet callback that mounts a CardView.
- Server-side worker: listens for optimistic tool signals and prefetches OAuth tokens in parallel, storing them in a short-lived cache keyed by signal.tool_id.

Observed telemetry and safety knobs
- Track: optimistic_signal_emitted, signal_confirmed_by_toolcall, snippet_schema_mismatch, snippet_partial_retries, prewarm_cancelled.
- Safety caps: ability to globally disable optimistic pre-warms for a customer (billing/safety).
- Cost estimation header: server returns a heuristic cost_estimate for pre-warm to surface to admin consoles.

Operational behavior and rollout plan
- Phase 0 (experiment): SDK flag opt-in for internal teams only; collect telemetry for 2 weeks.
- Phase 1 (limited beta): open to selected customers; add hooks to Redwood Console to visualize optimistic signals and pre-warm metrics.
- Phase 2 (GA): enable by default with conservative TTLs and cost controls; publish migration guide and examples.

Backward compatibility and integration notes
- Existing streaming clients: ignore unknown chunk types. New typed-snippet chunks will be treated as opaque strings unless SDK is upgraded.
- Gatekeeping: default API behavior is optimistic_tool_mode=disabled for all existing customers to avoid surprises.

Open questions (engineering + product)
- What precise confidence threshold should trigger an optimistic-tool-signal? (suggestion: 0.6 for beta)
- How to represent complex tool intents (multi-tool graphs) without exploding signal payload size?
- TTL tradeoffs: short TTL reduces cost but increases chance of missing actual tool calls.
- Native mobile vs web differences: should we expose different prewarm cost estimates?

Implementation notes (engineering backlog)
- Serving runtime: small emitter path to insert optimistic signals pre-KV commit; ensure idle hedging does not double-count token cost.
- Console: add visualizer for optimistic signal timeline and mapping to final toolcalls.
- SDK: JS + mobile (iOS/Android) baseline with async callbacks; provide example integrations for React Native and SwiftUI.
- Evals: create prompt harness that measures snippet fidelity and signal precision/recall.

Appendix: shorthand examples
- Streaming sequence (toy):
  - text chunk: "Here's a summary..."
  - optimistic-tool-signal: {tool_id: search-v2, intent: "firmographics", confidence: 0.78}
  - typed-snippet (partial): {id: s1, schema: cards.v1, partial: true, payload: "{\"title\":\"ACME\"...}"}
  - typed-snippet (final): {id: s1, schema: cards.v1, partial: false, payload: "..."}
  - final text chunk: "Done."

Summary
- This PRD proposes a narrowly-scoped, low-risk mechanism to improve streaming developer experience by delivering typed, incremental fragments and a best-effort tool-preparation signal.
- If the experiment demonstrates improved end-to-end perceived latency and reduced UI jitter for customers, we can iterate toward stronger transactional tool-call semantics.

Next steps
- Align with runtime on a minimal chunk envelope and wire a short POC (server + JS SDK) within two sprints.
- Run internal integration test with mobile team and one pilot customer.
- Revisit confidence thresholds and TTLs after first telemetry sweep.

Notes to reviewers
- This is a working draft. please add concrete SDK examples and small snippets showing error handling in the onOptimisticTool callback.
- Annotate any security/billing concerns inline (especially around prewarm cost signals).
